examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify scope and storage duration before tracing calls. Automatic locals are separate in each invocation; static locals retain one value across calls; a block declaration can shadow a parameter. Passing a pointer by value copies an address while still allowing writes to its object. Heap allocations require an explicit lifetime and ownership policy.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
f has static int x=2 and returns ++x. Three calls execute sequentially. What is the sum of their return values?

**Answer: 12.** The static variable persists: the calls return 3,4,5. Their sum is 12. Reinitializing x on every call would incorrectly give 9.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A pointer to an automatic local becomes invalid after its lifetime ends. Leaking an allocation and dereferencing a dangling pointer are different bugs.

A pointer remaining non-null after free does not mean its storage is still valid.
